articles.title: Selena Gomez’s Reaction To Martin Short Accidentally Cutting Her Wedding Cake Is As Funny As I’d Hoped
articles.summary: She couldn't have had a better reaction.
articles.content:
It's been well established that Selena Gomez , Martin Short and Steve Martin know how to get into hilarious trouble on Only Murders in the Building , which you can stream with a Hulu subscription . However, the members of the unexpected trio know how to do that in real life too. Need an example? Look no further than the time Martin Short accidentally cut Gomez's wedding cake , and her hilarious reaction to it.

I do love that Short tried his hardest to cover it up, but I can’t say I blame him for cutting into the cake. He revealed that there were different sections at the reception with couches and groups of people, and he simply thought there was a cake in each section.

Considering how close Gomez and Short have become over the years, I love that there were no hard feelings over the accidental cake cutting. It also further proves why they’re bestie goals . Even now, she laughed the entire time retelling the story, which Short says he is “blameless” in.

The friendship between Short, Martin, and Gomez is definitely the best thing to come out of Only Murders in the Building . Of course, Short and Martin have long been friends, but I definitely feel like Gomez was the missing piece. Now, I hope there are many more funny stories like this to come.

articles.title: 'The Mummy': Top Artifact Props From 1999 Film Heading to Auction Ahead of Franchise Revival (Exclusive)

articles.content:
Two signature props from 1999's franchise-launching The Mummy are set for auction ahead of the film series' forthcoming return to cinemas.

Propstore's Winter Entertainment Memorabilia Live Auction runs Dec. 4-6 and features a number of items from the film that starred Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz , The Hollywood Reporter has learned. These include the mechanical Hamunaptra Key, the complicated puzzle box protecting the map to the City of the Dead, and the mechanical Book of the Dead, which Rick (Fraser) and Evelyn (Weisz) inadvertently use to resurrect Imhotep. Seen below, the Hamunaptra Key is an octagonal item that, when its upper half is twisted, features eight panels that pop open in a sunburst design. In director Stephen Sommers' film, it was used to lock and unlock the Book of the Dead and the Book of Amun-Ra.

The Book of the Dead, also pictured below, is one of the defining Egyptian artifact props from the movie. It features an ornate mechanical lock and 12 tablet pages detailed with hieroglyphs, with the book's clasps capable of being released by twisting a circular emblem on the cover.

Registration and online bidding have opened for the auction that spans more than 1,400 lots. Among the highlights is Batman's Batpod from Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight and The Dark Knight Rises , with the motorbike receiving an opening bid of $598,000. The sale of the props from The Mummy come as the franchise revs up for a theatrical revival. Universal is set to release directors Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett's The Mummy: Book of the Dead in theaters on Oct. 15, 2027. Brendan Fraser, Rachel Weisz and John Hannah will reprise their franchise roles in the movie that is a sequel to the 1999 film and its 2001 follow-up, The Mummy Returns .

During a conversation with THR timed to the first film's 25th anniversary, Sommers noted his appreciation that The Mummy has continued to draw fans. "It's so funny how it just never went away," he said at the time. "I hate to say it, but somehow it's endeared itself to a lot of people."

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Initial sales numbers for Grand Theft Auto 6 have now been revealed by developer Rockstar Games, and they're absolutely staggering. Leading up to the launch of GTA 6 , it was already known that the game was going to be a surefire hit. By all viewable metrics pre-launch, GTA 6 was poised to not only be one of the biggest video games ever, but could also shatter records for the entertainment industry at large. Now, after merely one day on the market, we know that Rockstar achieved this goal.

In a new press release , Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, revealed that Grand Theft Auto 6 has already sold over 32.5 million copies. This total is based purely on units sold pre-release, too, which means that this tally has undoubtedly only gone up. As a result, this has led to Rockstar bringing in an astounding $3.79 billion in sales on day-one. This not only sets a new record for a video game launch, but also validates that GTA 6 is the biggest entertainment release ever across all mediums.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI ," said Rockstar president Sam Houser of the game's launch. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you."

In an unprecedented move Laika is giving back to the Portland Oregon community where the film not only was made, but also is set.

This Thanksgiving weekend , specifically on November 29, the studio will open the doors and invite local audiences to complimentary screenings all across town. So far 15 theatres adding up to 7900 seats and 37+ showings have already signed on and that number is expected to grow substantially. The idea to do this citywide free event actually came from its legendary six time-Oscar nominated cinematographer Caleb Deschanel who spent a good deal of time in Portland making the stop motion epic directed by Travis Knight who is also CEO of Laika. Portland has been one of the top grossing markets for the film - seven of the top ten markets are in the city - but rather than continuing to make residents pay to see their moment of cinema glory, Laika is offering the chance for everyone to see it for free. articles.title: Free Nintendo Switch Online Promotion Announced by Nintendo
articles.summary: A free Nintendo Switch Online promotion has been announced by Nintendo, letting Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 users snag three months of Nintendo Switch Online for free. Nintendo Switch Online at the monthly rate costs $4 a month, so this represents a savings of $12. This may not seem like much money, but right […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A free Nintendo Switch Online promotion has been announced by Nintendo, letting Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 users snag three months of Nintendo Switch Online for free. Nintendo Switch Online at the monthly rate costs $4 a month, so this represents a savings of $12. This may not seem like much money, but right now, just on the Nintendo eShop, $12 gets you games like Slay the Spire , Persona 4 Golden , and LEGO Harry Potter Collection. Further, in an economy where a simple candy bar costs over $2, any bit of money that can be saved quickly adds up.

In addition to some Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake freebies , Nintendo Switch Online subscribers on both Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 have until December 6th to get a 3-month free extension to their Nintendo Switch Online subscription when they purchase 12 months of a subscription. This 12 month subscription can be a brand new subscription as well as an extension to a pre-exisiting subscription itself.

Right now, the offer is limited to the UK . Whether it will come to the United States and other markets remains to be seen, but there's a decent chance it will. If not, there are ways to take advantage of the deal without actually being in the UK. Meanwhile, this offer is not only available with the standard tier, but the Expansion Pack tier as well. The Expansion Pack is not available monthly. It can only be purchased at the 12-month rate, which costs $50. Effectively it's a similar amount of savings compared to three months of the monthly subscription to the standard tier, which is marked up in price because it's not 12 months bundeled.

It's quite rare for Nintendo to runs promotions on Nintendo Switch Online, even during the holiday season. Nintendo Switch Online is already very cheap compared to PlayStation Plus and Xbox Game Pass, so there likely isn't much wiggle room to run these type of promotions. Whatever the reason why, the point is these type of NSO promotions don't happen very often, so those who can should take advantage of this one while it's live and an option.

Nintendo Switch Online is available via Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2. Right now, there is no official word or rumblings of any major changes coming to the subscription service, such as a price increase, but it does look like a new console platform may be coming to NSO soon .

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Although Solo Leveling has remained quiet for a while, with no official release dates announced for any of its projects, the franchise's live-action series has just taken a promising step closer to release. Netflix's live-action adaptation was first announced in July 2025, featuring a promising cast and the surprising decision to follow the K-Drama format. Filming for the series, however, began in May this year, and so far, there have been two updates from the leading actors offering insight into how production is unfolding. It is safe to say that the project is aiming for an ambitious release and could become a live-action adaptation that fans will remember.

However, no release date or window has been officially announced as of this writing. A report from Financial News , however, may have just confirmed a 2028 release window for the series. South Korean entertainment and production company CJ ENM recently celebrated the 10th anniversary of one of its programs, O'PEN, which supports aspiring screenwriters, songwriters, and, more recently, novelists. The announcement emerged from one of the program's writers, who is speculated to also be involved in writing Netflix's Solo Leveling live-action K-Drama. A closer look at the details makes the potential 2028 release window for this project all the more plausible.

Considering that filming for the live-action adaptation only began in May this year, and the latest update from actress Han So-hee, who plays Cha Hae-in , suggests that filming is still underway, there is still some time before production comes to an end. It is evident that a significant amount of effort will go into post-production to bring the series' fantastical elements to life. This will require the production company to dedicate a considerable amount of time, especially considering that the first season will consist of seven episodes. Since it is also following the K-Drama format, fans can expect longer episodes, with the first season potentially covering a major portion of the story, perhaps reaching the point covered by the anime's first two seasons.

This gives the anonymous report from Financial News much more credibility. With this, Solo Leveling has finally secured a potential release window for a visual project for the first time since the anime concluded in 2025. There is no doubt that the most ambitious upcoming project is the anime movie, Solo Leveling: Beyond the System , which will immediately follow the anime and precede its third season. However, there is still no confirmed release date for the movie, despite fans speculating that it could arrive next year.

That said, there is still a possibility that the anime movie could be the next project fans get to see, potentially arriving in late 2027 or early 2028. Either way, these promising updates suggest that after two years of silence in the visual and audio formats, the Solo Leveling franchise is preparing for major releases over the next couple of years, once again capturing the industry's attention and potentially breaking even more records upon its return.

articles.title: 5 Marvel Superheroes Whose Origin Stories Were Altered Beyond Recognition
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Marvel Comics has created some of the most iconic origin stories in the comic book industry. These origins often show heroes not only gaining incredible powers but also learning important life lessons. However, these origin stories have often been altered. Some of these alterations are as simple as updating the origin stories for the modern […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics has created some of the most iconic origin stories in the comic book industry. These origins often show heroes not only gaining incredible powers but also learning important life lessons. However, these origin stories have often been altered. Some of these alterations are as simple as updating the origin stories for the modern day. Other times, a superhero’s origin story is changed so dramatically that it’s practically unrecognizable from how they initially debuted. These changes have ranged from highly controversial to making these heroes even more complex and groundbreaking. When these changes happened, everything we thought we knew about our favorite Marvel heroes was revealed to be a lie.

Writers are always trying to leave their mark on Marvel’s biggest characters. One surefire way to do this is to add new layers to the heroes’ backstories.

The superhero twins Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver have been the subject of numerous messy retcons that toyed with their true parentage. Although their origin was kept secret for years, it was eventually revealed that they were the mutant children of Golden Age heroes Miss America and the Whizzer. Marvel writers almost immediately scrapped that origin, instead making the twins the illegitimate children of Magneto. This revelation made much more narrative sense and lent itself to plenty of great stories centered on familial drama. However, because the twins couldn’t be portrayed as mutants in the MCU , Marvel Comics changed their origin yet again. Instead of being Magneto's mutant children, Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver were made to be children kidnapped by the High Evolutionary and used in his mad experiments, which gave them powers. This retcon has since proven especially controversial, as it undoes a great deal of character development for Magneto, Scarlet Witch, and Quicksilver.

When he first debuted, Bruce Banner was portrayed as a brilliant yet average scientist who was exposed to gamma bomb radiation, turning him into a giant beast. Originally, the Jolly Green Giant was treated as a straightforward monster that was born from gamma radiation. However, later writers revealed that the Hulk was part of Bruce long before the gamma bomb. As it turned out, Bruce was abused by his father, David Banner, and developed a dissociative identity disorder. The Hulk was a split personality and the personification of Bruce’s suppressed rage. The radiation only gave the Hulk a physical form. Later, it would be revealed that Bruce and the Hulk were empowered not just by radiation, but by the all-powerful, malevolent One Below All that rests at the bottom of the multiverse. These retcons turned the Hulk from a classic monster into a creature drenched in both psychological and cosmic horror.

Professor X always tries to recruit more mutants into the X-Men, but there was one roster he made sure everyone would forget. The All-New, All-Different X-Men team, including heroes like Wolverine, Nightcrawler, and Storm, was first brought together by Professor X to save the original five X-Men, who had been trapped on the living island of Krakoa. However, it was later revealed that this new team was Professor X’s second attempt to rescue Krakoa. Beforehand, he had an entirely different X-Men team consisting of the mutants Kid Vulcan, Petra, Darwin, and Sway. The mission was a complete disaster and it was assumed that Krakoa and its monsters had killed every member of that team. To cover up the tragedy, Professor X mind-wiped everyone so no one would remember that the second X-Men team and its members ever existed. This action was made even worse by the fact that Kid Vulcan was Cyclops’s brother Gabriel. This reveal warped people’s perception of Professor X from a kind, selfless teacher to a master manipulator.

A huge part of Spider-Man’s appeal is how seemingly random his origin was. Peter Parker just happened to be in the right place at the right time when a radioactive spider bit him. However, later writers would introduce the idea that Peter was destined to become Spider-Man, and that it wasn’t even the radiation that gave him powers. This idea would be explored with the introduction of Ezekiel, who also had spider-based powers. He explained that he and Peter were both Spider-Totems, who are avatars of the Great Weaver. This mystical and cosmic entity spins the Web of Life that connects all worlds in the multiverse. Peter, along with nearly every other spider-based hero in existence, acts as a champion of the Great Weaver. Peter actively suppresses the full power that his status as a Spider-Totem provides so that he can retain his humanity. This retcon has been incredibly controversial, but it also led to the concept of the Spider-Verse .

At first glance, Thor’s origin as Odin's banished son seems simple. However, when Thor first appeared in Marvel Comics, he wasn’t even a god. Initially, Dr. Donald Blake was just a mortal man who found a stick inside a cave. When Donald grabbed it, he was transformed into Thor. The early comics made it clear that the “Thor” we saw was just Donald, given the powers and appearance of the God of Thunder. Over time, the line between Donald and Thor blurred over whether he was mortal or a god. These narrative inconsistencies culminated in Thor #159, four years after the characters’ debut, when Odin revealed the truth. It turned out that Odin had banished Thor to Earth, turning him into the mortal Donald Blake with no memory of his past. Not only would Thor abandon his mortal form and secret identity, but he and Donald would eventually become fully independent individuals.

articles.title: MrBeast Settles Lawsuit Against Ex-Dev Director Over Allegedly Swiped Files and Hidden Cameras
articles.summary: The former employee oversaw issues ranging from content production to fundraising to political advocacy.
articles.content:
MrBeast has settled a lawsuit from a former development director who allegedly stole internal company documents and installed hidden cameras at company offices.

Lawyers for MrBeast and the ex-employee, Leroy Nabors, told the court on Friday of a deal to resolve the case. Under the agreement, he'll submit to a forensic inspection of his devices and accounts to ensure that sensitive information has been removed and not been disclosed.

"Upon satisfactory completion of the Protocol, Beast will voluntarily dismiss this action," states the filing. The dismissal will be "without prejudice," meaning the lawsuit can be refiled.

Nabors started at the company in 2023 as an IT contractor before becoming head of the development team. Upon learning that he'd be fired, he allegedly swiped thousands of documents containing financial data and sensitive information regarding business transactions and company investors, plus blueprints detailing how the social media superstar develops megahit videos, among other intellectual property.

Nabors later wiped his laptop to cover his tracks, according to the complaint. When he was confronted by the company about the alleged theft, he said that the mass download was a routine "backup" he conducted in the "normal course of business" and refused to return the documents, the lawsuit said

In its investigation, MrBeast said it discovered multiple hidden cameras across its offices and a device attached to its servers containing an application that allows users to remotely access and control its network. The company suspects Labors to have installed them. Nabors' daughter contracted with MrBeast to manage its entire IT network and had access to the camera feeds, according to the complaint.

MrBeast brought claims for misappropriation of trade secrets and breach of contract, among others. It sought unspecified damages.

The lawsuit detailed some of the innerworkings of the media empire controlled by MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson. It described the company's development team as "deliberately flexible and multi-purpose, tackling issues ranging from content production to fundraising to political advocacy." The company maintains strict security protocols, limiting access to trade secrets to certain employees and storing such information in a separate network, according to the complaint. It routinely audits user access to critical shared folders and directs employees to regularly change their passwords, said the lawsuit, which noted that applications on company devices require user authentication and have a session timeout mechanism.

A " Home Alone " sequel is in early development at Disney , Variety has confirmed. Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg are shaping the script with original star Macaulay Culkin and will produce through their Point Grey banner.

Plot details and further casting remain under wraps. Disney declined to comment.

The original "Home Alone" premiered in 1990 and starred a nine-year-old Culkin as Kevin McCallister, the youngest of many in the McCallister household who wishes he never had to see his family again after a rough night packing for Christmas vacation. Kevin gets his wish when the McCallister clan forgets to wake him on the way to the airport. Kevin is forced to become the man of the house, and in the third act he must fend off the holiday burglars known as the Wet Bandits. Joe Pesci and Daniel Stern co-starred as the bumbling thieves. articles.title: Fired Home Alone Star Sad ‘Every Christmas’ He Has To ‘Put Up’ With More Stories About What Happened
articles.summary: It’s not such a merry Christmas.
articles.content:
Home Alone is one of the most beloved Christmas movies ever. Families watch and rewatch it every year around the holidays. For most, it’s a celebratory time, but for one actor, Daniel Roebuck, it’s bittersweet. Roebuck, if you didn’t know (and I didn’t), was the original actor cast in the role of one of the Wet Bandits, Marv, who was memorably played by Daniel Stern. Behind the scenes of Home Alone , Roebuck was fired by director Chris Columbus just four days into filming, and ever since, Christmas has meant he has to relive that tough moment.

Roebuck has had a busy career since, including big roles in movies like The Fugitive and Agent Cody Banks , but he never worked with Columbus again.

This all stemmed from a story Columbus recently recounted about filming Home Alone on The Wildmen Podcast , where the director explained that the studio would only pay for either Daniel Stern or Joe Pesci (who played Marv’s partner Harry), but not both. So Roebuck was cast and, according to Columbus, the first screen test with Roebuck and Pesci was “terrible.” Roebuck, however, disputes that version of the story, telling PageSix:

He added that he only worked with Pesci for one day. He also adds that, despite Columbus telling him they would work together (something Columbus also notes), that never happened, and they haven’t spoken since. Roebuck still doesn’t understand the reasoning behind his firing, but he doesn’t have any ill will towards Columbus, saying:

Ultimately, though, Roebuck didn’t star in the movie, and, at least according to Columbus, the director got the actor he wanted all along. It’s pretty hard to imagine the movie without Stern , but these events bring a little bit of a dark cloud over the casting. I guess in the end, Columbus did what he thought he had to do, but it’s easy to understand why Roebuck has mixed feelings about what many consider one of the best Christmas movies ever.

articles.content:
Candle Media cofounder Kevin Mayer told an industry conference in Doha on Friday that he had not foreseen the impending contraction in demand for streaming content ahead of the company’s launch in 2021.

He was speaking six weeks after Candle Media hit the trade headlines for its sale of Reece Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine to Paris-based European content group Mediawan.

Candle Media originally acquired the company, behind Big Little Lies and The Morning Show , in 2021, as one of its first acquisitions for $900M. Mayer, who was talking on to the Qatar Film Committee’s Industry Days event in Doha via video-link from L.A., did not dwell on the sale.

“On the live action side, we gave it a really good shot with Hella Sunshine and other assets. It was okay, but they didn't work out to what we wanted, so we recently sold those,” he said.

Mayer did not go into details on why Hello Shine had not worked out for Candle Media, and there were no opportunities for questions from the floor.

His wide discussion, however, gave some insight into some of the challenges facing the company as well as triumphs led by its acquisition of Moonbug , the children’s media company behind shows such as CoComelon , Blippi and Little Ange l.

The former Disney exec, who oversaw the studio's 2019 acquisition of 20th Century Fox and also helped spearhead the creation of Disney+ alongside Bon Iger, said the idea for Candle Media had been sparked by the studios getting into streaming and taking their IP in-house.

This trend, he said, suggested that streamers without big inhouse production capacity would be on the hunt for high-quality content.

"We felt that the value of being independent in that sort of industry, that vertically integrated, would be increasing, and I think that is still true. Being independent and having that that ability to sell to any of the streaming services is great,” he said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“We also thought content demand would continue to increase double digits a year… with increasing demand globally for high-quality content, like we were producing at Candle Media, which would provide us with the volume we needed to make all of our acquisitions work financially,” he continued.

“Starting in 2023, that didn't happen. In fact, the demand for streaming content actually contracted quite a bit, to about 35% below the peak of 2022. So, that part of our thesis was incorrect, unfortunately. We didn't see that contraction coming.”

The second premise on which the company was built, he said, was the belief that strong IP and stories could exist on multiple formats.

“They could exist on YouTube and on TikTok and on other platforms as short form entertainment… they could coexist in traditional film, on streaming and television and elsewhere,” he said. “Then they would open up other revenue platforms such as consumer products licensing, which we did a lot with Disney, games, music…”

Mayer pointed to children’s media company Moonbug, which Candle Media acquired in 2021, as having fulfilled that gaol thanks to shows like CoCocomelon, which was born on YouTube, and then repackaged for Netflix.

“We took those stories that came from YouTube, put them into one-hour compilations and licensed them to Netflix from 2021 to 2024. While CoComelon was the largest YouTube channel in the world, it was also the most popular Netflix show in the world. For three solid years, it was the number one streaming show and the number one YouTube show," he said.

He said the operation had not worked in the opposite direction for more traditional IP.

“We were hopeful that we could take traditional film and TV and cross it over into social media. That didn't work all that well. But what did work really well is taking social media storytelling and crossing it over to traditional. And you've seen Obsession and Backrooms … all this stuff is happening from that perspective.”

articles.title: Does Niko Bellic Return in GTA 6? Everything We Know About “The Hitman”
articles.summary: One of the biggest questions that has surrounded Grand Theft Auto 6 since its launch is surprisingly tied to Niko Bellic, the main protagonist from Grand Theft Auto 4. While Niko hasn't been seen in the Grand Theft Auto series since the conclusion of GTA 4, many wondered if he would potentially appear in the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the biggest questions that has surrounded Grand Theft Auto 6 since its launch is surprisingly tied to Niko Bellic, the main protagonist from Grand Theft Auto 4 . While Niko hasn't been seen in the Grand Theft Auto series since the conclusion of GTA 4 , many wondered if he would potentially appear in the latest installment in the series. After all, past GTA games have brought back other characters from the franchise's history, which certainly made it possible for Niko to have a cameo of some sort.

These questions surrounding Niko Bellic only grew louder when fans noticed that his character's voice actor, Michael Hollick, appeared in the cast list for GTA 6 . However, Hollick isn't mentioned in the credits of GTA 6 as portraying Bellic, but instead, a character known only as "The Hitman". Just who is The Hitman, though, and how does he play part in

WARNING: Spoilers for GTA 6 are mentioned from this point forward in this article. Read onward at your own discretion.

In short, yes, Niko Bellic does appear in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Niko appears relatively late in the main story of GTA 6 , as he ends up crossing paths with Jason and Lucia. He's aged quite a bit since we last saw him, with Niko even mentioning that he hasn't killed anyone since 2012. This suggests that he may have been able to briefly get away from his life of crime, which was his goal at the end of GTA 4 , but he ultimately got pulled back in.

As a whole, Niko doesn't end up being in GTA 6 very much. He only appears in two of the game's scenes in Chapter 5, the first of which is titled "Taking Liberties." In addition to his short screen time, Niko is joined by some of the music that was heard in GTA 4 . This makes his appearance all the more nostalgic for those who have been playing Grand Theft Auto for the better part of the past 20 years.

As for the reason behind Niko being referred to as "The Hitman" in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6 , it's because that's his brief role in the game. When Niko first shows up, it's at the penthouse of Giorgio Gallo, who is one of the biggest crime lords in Vice City. Giorgio works in tandem with a European mafia to ship billions of dollars of drugs across the globe, but when he makes a mistake that results in said drugs being confiscated by the United States government, Niko arrives to take him out as a punishment for his error.

Ultimately, Niko agrees to give Giorgio one more chance to rectify his mistake. This results in him enlisting Lucia and Jason to help steal back the confiscated drugs. Once Lucia and Jason complete this mission, Niko shows up once again and is stunned that they were able to pull off such a difficult heist. He then mentions that he's now going to head back home, which is an obvious reference to his own residence within Liberty City.

Even though Niko never actually kills anyone in Grand Theft Auto 6 , it's clear that Rockstar chose to call him "The Hitman" in the game's credits just to preserve the surprise nature of his appearance. His brief cameo is one of the biggest moments in the entirety of GTA 6 and helps make the larger Grand Theft Auto saga feel a bit more cohesive.

articles.summary: Fifty years ago, Sylvester Stallone’s movie about an underdog boxer toppled films like ‘Taxi Driver’ and ‘All the President’s Men’ at the Oscars.
articles.content:
If you want to know the behind-the-scenes story of how Sylvester Stallone got Rocky into theaters, check out I Play Rocky , opening nationwide Nov. 20, just one day shy of the original film's 50th anniversary. How Stallone typed up a screenplay in just a few days. How he waved away piles of money in order to star in the picture himself, despite the studio insisting on a bigger name (like, say, Burt Reynolds, Ryan O'Neal or Clint Eastwood). How shooting that beef-beating scene in the meat locker left Stallone with bloody fists and busted knuckles. All that and more is faithfully re-enacted in Peter Farrelly's new backstage biopic. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Golden Globes Category Chaos: When 'The Drama' Is a Comedy... What's not in the film, though, is what happened after Rocky 's Nov. 21, 1976, New York opening, which in some ways is just as incredible an underdog story. With no stars (except Burgess Meredith) and virtually no budget (even 50 years ago, a million dollars was a pittance in Hollywood), Rocky had no business becoming the biggest film of the year. But it ended up drawing blockbuster crowds — with audiences cheering as if ringside at a real boxing match — ultimately grossing $225 million worldwide, or about $1.3 billion in today's dollars.

Then there was round two, Oscar night. At the 49th Academy Awards , Rocky beat Network , Taxi Driver , All the President's Men and Bound for Glory for best picture, and also picked up a best director statuette for John G. Avildsen. Stallone himself went home empty-handed, as did his three nominated co-stars, Talia Shire, Meredith and Burt Young. articles.title: 'Best Pancakes in the County' Review: Nicolas Cage Goes Gonzo, Again, in a Dismal Action-Comedy That Fails to Match His Energy
articles.summary: A remote diner is the setting for Ken Sanzel's movie featuring a stand-off between corrupt FBI agents and a gang of criminals.
articles.content:
You have to admire Nicolas Cage ’s penchants for loyalty and consistency. His latest effort reunites him with director-screenwriter Ken Sanzel, with whom he previously collaborated on 2019’s Kill Chain , a film that few saw and even fewer liked. And it features the sort of gonzo trademark Cage performance for which he’s become both admired and ridiculed, in this case featuring a degree of misplaced commitment to the bit that definitely doesn’t pay off. The only saving grace of Best Pancakes in the County is the excellent recipe advice about the titular food that will definitely improve your breakfast gatherings. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Nicolas Cage on His Approach to Playing John Madden in New Biopic: "I'm Not an Impressionist" Movies 'Madden' Review: Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale Go for Broke in a Cartoonish Biopic From David O. Russell That's Strictly for Football Fanatics

This is the sort of movie that is routinely described as “Tarantinoesque” (a word that’s actually included in the Oxford English Dictionary, don’t you know) thanks to its convoluted plotting, eccentric characters, jokey dialogue, and propensity for Mexican standoffs. These movies are, with a few exceptions, invariably bad, but this one takes the pancake. Best Pancakes in the County The Bottom Line The worst movie in the multiplex. Release date : Friday, November 20 Cast : Nicolas Cage, Justin Long, Shelley Hennig, Ravi Patel, Brandon Mychal Smith, Lauren German, Kelly Greyson Director-screenwriter : Ken Sanzel 1 hour 38 minutes

Cage clearly participated in creating the look for his character, labeled in an onscreen graphic as “The Son of a Bitch.” Playing a ruthless criminal who doesn’t hesitate to shoot his partner while eating ice cream after a safe-cracking burglary goes awry, the actor wears hideous ‘70s-era clothes and a terrible perm wig, his make-up featuring extensive facial scarring and a porcine nose. He also employs a speaking style that sounds like he inhaled helium before every take.

After a prologue in which the S.O.B. steals a MacGuffin, excuse me, hard drive, from an FBI stash house, the bulk of the action takes place in a diner whose only employees are Cookie ( Justin Long , once again working hard in subpar material), the cook, and Dolly (Shelley Hennig), a waitress whose specialty is the breakfast item described in the title. The diner, surreptitiously owned by the S.O.B., is located precisely in the middle of nowhere. But that doesn’t prevent it from soon being visited by a large number of patrons — including the S.O.B.’s criminal associates led by Ryder ( Ravi Patel , seen to much better effect in the sitcom Animal Control ) and a cadre of corrupt FBI agents headed by tough-talking Agent Margot (Lauren German). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Much violent mayhem ensues, including many characters getting gunned down by a drone armed with an automatic weapon. None of it is remotely convincing, however, with the obviously low-budget film featuring the fakest looking CGI blood spatter effects this side of a ‘90s-era video game, and a final shootout shot so darkly you can’t make out what’s going on. Throughout it all the characters make jocular asides, with one series of exchanges relying on the notion that the phrase “hummus wrap” is inherently amusing. Needless to say, there are also plot twists, albeit ones you can see from a mile away, including the revelation that Cookie and Dolly aren’t exactly whom they appear to be.

Cage, absent from the proceedings for long stretches, gives it all and then some, to the point that you can feel his delight upon repeatedly uttering the phrase “I can’t find my thumb!” after a particularly gruesome incident. You half expect him to reprise his line “I’m Nicolas friggin’ Cage!” from The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent .

His efforts, as gonzo as they are, are all for naught, with the movie’s incoherent plotting, risible dialogue, and subpar filmmaking making it a torturous experience with nothing memorable about it other than its title. That the distributor doesn’t have much confidence in its prospects is evident from its simultaneous release in “select” theaters and availability on digital platforms.

articles.title: Jean Grey Has Finally Lost Everything, and It's a Perfect Reversal of Her Most Iconic X-Men Story
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Jean Grey's most famous story, without a doubt, is "The Dark Phoenix Saga." It's a tragic tale that still echoes […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Jean Grey's most famous story, without a doubt, is "The Dark Phoenix Saga." Her fall from grace, as the full might of her cosmic powers possessed her, led her to destroy an entire planet and, eventually, take her own life to keep the same thing from happening again. It's a tragic tale that still echoes throughout the X-Men comics today, especially since Jean has returned from the dead more often than not. In fact, she dies and returns so often that it's become something of a character trope, where Marvel must kill off Jean every so many years to meet a quota. Now, however, Jean isn't the character to die. Rather, she's the one left to pick up the pieces.

As of DNX #5, Cyclops seemingly died in his battle against the evil version of the Beast, the Chairman. Unbeknownst to everyone, Scott was actually saved or revived by the Chairman, but to the world, he's dead. Given their special psychic rapport, Jean knew immediately that her husband was gone, and now she's left to pick up the pieces of his death as she rockets towards Earth in fury and grief . This is one seriously compelling storyline, and one that harkens back to the most common criticisms of Jean's character.

Jean has died a lot in comics. Her first and most famous death was, of course, her noble sacrifice in "The Dark Phoenix Saga," and that was planned to be her final resting place, but this is comics, so nobody stays dead forever. Her return in X-Factor (1986) broke the seal on that, and after she died once more in Chris Claremont's legendary New X-Men (2001) run, the precedent had been set. Jean's death was always meant to serve as a major moment for the X-Men that would push them into a new era, just like her resurrections would. With that in mind, Marvel decided to repeatedly bring back Jean temporarily over the next decade and a half, only to kill her once again, calling back to these important deaths with less impact each time.

Jean hasn't died as many times as people meme about, but she certainly has passed from this realm more than the average character, and that has left its impact. Most notably, the character who faces the biggest challenges and changes when Jean dies is always Scott. He's repeatedly watched the love of his life give herself up for the greater good and vanish, leaving him to figure out how to keep moving forward . The majority of Scott's biggest pivots and developments come from moving on from Jean's deaths. Even his hard turn to mutant terrorism sparked from his brush with the Phoenix Force, for crying out loud.

This newest story, however, completely reverses this dynamic. For the first time, Jean has lost Scott, and now she has to live knowing that she might never see him again. He isn't bound to the cosmic embodiment of resurrection, nor do the X-Men have access to Krakoa's ability to cheat death anymore. Jean will have to face this grief and agony as a survivor, and that's incredibly dangerous. At the end of the day, Scott is a man who will always bury his emotions, and even when he loses control and cuts loose, at best he could bring down a mountain. Jean's power is built around control. She could throw the world out of alignment with a thought, and now she's facing the worst feeling she's ever had.

This new direction for Jean is definitely something her character has needed. The shift to her facing cosmic threats and traveling the universe, battling villains like Thanos, has been interesting, but it's also disconnected her from the relationships that people love. Namely, her marriage with Scott. But X-Men (2024) is about to change that, bringing Jean back to Earth without brushing aside her status as an undisputed universe-ending threat. This storyline has been set up since the very beginning, with Scott openly telling O.N.E. agents that, if anything happened to him, Jean would come back to Earth in a blaze of fury. He's been dropping these kinds of threats since issue #3, and said it explicitly in issue #10.

The first real step is stopping Jean from pulling a Dark Phoenix and destroying the Earth, which has been explicitly called out several times. Kid Omega is on the team for that exact purpose , according to Cyclops's own words from issue #10. Obviously, the team will talk her down before it gets to that, and Jean's new status quo will be learning how to live back on Earth without Scott. He was the one who kept the X-Men together. Without Xavier around to connect everyone through his dream, it fell to Scott, and now to Jean, to act in his stead. Scott was the X-Men's greatest leader, but Jean will have to be something else entirely: their heart.

She's far from the only one grieving Cyclops. Beast will take it especially hard, and the rest of the X-Men will be lost and directionless. Jean will have to remind them exactly why they fight the fight. She won't be giving speeches about mutually assured destruction or creating an endless number of contingency plans, but she will remind the X-Men of the humanity that their stories are all too often distant from. Jean's new direction will need to give her the chance to reconnect not just with the planet, but its people. The reason her deaths have always been such massive moments in X-history is that she represents the soul that inspires them to keep going when logic has failed. She'll have to learn how to be that once again in a world that has moved on without her, and how to pull everyone together when the beast inside of her wants to rip it all apart.

What do you think will be the main focus of Jean's arc going forward? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.summary: Sebastian Stan's Bucky Barnes will get new gear once again in the MCU this December. It's no surprise that Marvel's superheroes are getting an upgrade for Avengers: Doomsday. Not only is it tradition at this point for characters to have a new style of totally different costume for any new movie or show (gotta sell […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Sebastian Stan's Bucky Barnes will get new gear once again in the MCU this December . It's no surprise that Marvel's superheroes are getting an upgrade for Avengers: Doomsday . Not only is it tradition at this point for characters to have a new style of totally different costume for any new movie or show (gotta sell those toys somehow), but it's pretty seldom that they actually change all that much. We already know that some characters in Doomsday will be going to their comic book roots , but others are getting a fresh upgrade.

Having been a part of the MCU since Captain America: The First Avenger in 2011, Sebastian Stan's Bucky has had a variety of looks over that time. New international posters for Avengers: Doomsday have started to make the rounds online, including one for Stan's Winter Soldier that reveals a new Avengers costume for the character, that marks his seventh superhero suit in the MCU. Check it out for yourself below, with the image revealing that he has brighter armor this time around, one that seems pearlescent, like the quantum suits worn in Endgame .

It's worth noting that in the poster above, Bucky's costume looks like the one he's seen wearing in the post-credit scene of last year's Thunderbolts . That scene is confirmed to have been shot on the set of Avengers: Doomsday , meaning that the looks the characters are sporting there are the same costumes they'll seemingly have on across the film. Despite this, the image does make it look like the armor on Bucky's costume is brighter, so there's a chance it's a slight variant from what we've already seen.

Across the MCU, Bucky may have one of the most eclectic ranges of superhero costumes compared to his co-stars. The First Avenger had him in somewhat traditional army fatigues, while he became The Winter Soldier in the 2014 sequel. Civil War gave him a slight upgrade, but his appearances in Black Panther and Avengers: Infinity War gave his signature metal arm a new look entirely. From there, he changed looks once again in the Disney+ series The Falcon and the Winter Soldier , plus in Thunderbolts *, which saw him in at least two different superhero costumes. Revisit them yourself below.

With less than a month to go before Avengers: Doomsday is released in theaters, we can expect even more teases and confirmations about the film to start trickling out into the world. Though another full trailer is still expected to arrive eventually, so far fans are only getting updates piecemeal from across the internet.

Earlier this week, some fresh footage arrived from Marvel in a BTS video about Robert Downey Jr.'s MCU return. Though it was light on new details, it did include the hidden update that Vanessa Kirby's Sue Storm is also getting a new superhero suit upgrade for Doomsday. Between that update and today's reveal of Bucky's duds, fans shouldn't be surprised if even more superheroes stop for a wardrobe change in between fights with the titular baddie.

The Bold Type co-executive producer Holly Whidden, a Nantucket insider who was a consulting producer on The Perfect Couple , also serves as executive producer.

Protagonists Jason Duval (Dylan Rourke) and Lucia Caminos (Manni L. Perez) have a son: Baby “Tommy” Tomas.

“GTA 6” opens with a flashback to a double-grand-theft-auto meet-cute between Jason and Lucia. He goes to steal a car that she’s already stolen, the cops come and love blooms. Through a montage of their relationship, we see their happy times and things fall apart as Lucia wants to get more involved in some of Jason’s criminal activities and he refuses to bring her along.

After the two seemingly split, we see Lucia sitting in a restaurant ordering only water when she decides to rob a payday loan shop across the street. She’s still living in their fictional state of Leonida (inspired by Florida), but she’s on her own and hurting for cash after being suspended from her rideshare driver job.

The crime is a bust, and we catch up to Lucia in present day, where she’s in prison for the attempted armed robbery. Cut back to the day when Lucia tried to rob the loan shop, and she’s seen screaming about how she needs to go back to the restaurant. It’s then revealed to players that Lucia left her infant son, Tomas, behind in the restaurant across the street and he’s crying, surrounded by restaurant employees while waiting for her to return.

From here, it’s up to “GTA 6” players to decide how they want Lucia and Jason (who in present day knows he has a son but has still never met him) to live their lives when they reunite upon her release. Tommy is in the custody of Lucia’s aunt, but will he stay that way, depending on how you play?

It started with Dragon Ball Super: Broly , where the Legendary Super Saiyan continued to display obscene levels of power without advancing to his next form . Super Dragon Ball Heroes then took it out of the stratosphere initially showing how strong Cumber was while still restrained in his base form.

People can say that it's a non-canon anime release , but Dragon Ball has a history of using non-canon elements in the canon's main story. Crazy enough, Cumber's first appearance in Super Dragon Ball Heroes was released before the new Broly film. So the concept was there before it officially made it into canon, just like Super Saiyan 4's path to canonization. With the direction the series is headed in, it feels like latent power might get more of a focus in the future.

A conversation that started back during Dragon Ball Z was latent potential. It started when Goku was addressed as a low-level fighter by Raditz and Vegeta . The term mostly references a fighter's untapped power that starts at a Saiyan's birth. Goku outgrew his expected poor power level and continues to prove that hard work and heart mean more than potential. However, it's not focused enough on how good a fighter could be, especially if they start at a higher base level like Broly and Cumber. The former was sent away for exactly that reason.

Cumber clearly boasts an insane potential. He stayed in his base form and depowered Super Saiyan Trunks, battled well with Super Saiyan Blue Vegito and never missed a beat. When he needed to finally transform, he only ascended to a Golden Great Ape and then later Super Saiyan 3 against Super Saiyan 4 Xeno Vegito. It was an insane display of power that made audiences rethink how latent abilities work into the equation. Furthermore, the non-canon iteration of Dragon Ball Z Broly showed off the power of Super Saiyan 4, despite that power-up being significantly outdated by timeline standards as well. He matched up with Super Saiyan 3 Cumber , proving that potential, not new transformations can reign supreme.

While Super Dragon Ball Heroes got the conversation started, it got continual help from the Broly film and then Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero . Maybe the biggest example of latent ability is none other than Gohan. Goku's son always carries a little more in the tank when it comes to fighting. As a small child, he was able to fight Raditz when his anger caused his power level to skyrocket. He later proved he could up his power level just a few years later against Super Perfect Cell as Gohan became the strongest fighter on Earth at that time.

He then stopped training, yet somehow managed to jump to the top of the power board in Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero by becoming Beast Gohan . It keeps the plot interesting as anyone can show up at anytime and quickly overpower the Z Fighters. It also keeps Goku and Vegeta training for that exact reason. The next threat is always right around the corner, especially when neither of them are the latent kings of the universe. Which makes things fun because they truly are the underdogs in every fight. Do you think Dragon Ball is embracing this concept well? Let us know in the comments.

Bowen Yang has apologized after he received backlash recently for calling singer Regina Spektor an antisemitic slur on a past episode of his podcast, "Las Culturistas." A resurfaced clip of the Oct. 14 episode of the podcast came under fire when Yang referred to Spektor as "Zio."

"I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we've repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks," Yang wrote on Instagram on Friday. "Particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Zio," short for "Zionist," has been used as a derogatory slur toward Jewish people and Israelis. Its origins trace back to Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke and white supremacists.

On the Oct. 14 episode of "Las Culturistas," Yang, his co-host Matt Rogers and guest Edy Modica were discussing Spektor, her alma mater SUNY Purchase and her music when Modica added, "And now she's out to lunch." Rogers asked if Modica was "upset with Regina lately," to which she responded, "she's just like a little Israel hardcore." Yang added, "yeah, she's Zio."

articles.summary: There's nothing you can take from her.
articles.content:
Happy Hunger Games! Sunrise on the Reaping is the latest book-to-screen adaptation to hit theaters, which means we finally get to see Haymitch compete in the games. We already knew there would be a lot of references to the original movies and throughout the press tour , but there's so many more talk of the events in The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes than we expected. One star just revealed another one that's barely in the movie, and it's kind of a big deal. SPOILERS AHEAD!

As you may recall, the end of The Songbirds and Snakes had Lucy Gray Baird disappearing into the forest, leaving President Snow betrayed and alone. We never knew what happened to her next. Enter a photo dump posted by Whitney Peak, who plays Lenore Dove in Sunrise on the Reaping . Check out the third photo below:

The photo has Sunrise on the Reaping 's Joseph Zada pointing to a gravestone. Here's what it says:

The stone was featured in the movie when Haymitch visits the grave of Lenore Dove, but we couldn't make out the words in the inscription until this photo. How poetic is it that Lucy Gray Baird and Lenore Dove's final resting places are right next to each other? The picture seems to solve the mystery of Lucy's body being found at some point. It would make sense given there's 40 years between the two prequels.

The gravestone heavily suggests Lucy Gray Baird was buried in the Covey graveyard, but since we only have a photo to go off of, there's still not a simple answer around what happened to Lucy. I looked around on a Reddit thread discussing the photo, and there's a lot interesting ideas floating around. Here's my favorite:

I think it absolutely makes sense that Lucy might have escaped, but ultimately wanted to come home at some point. There's something really sweet about imagining her going home to her Covey and living life among the others in peace after Snow was consumed by being the president of the Capitol. Here's another school of thought on the reveal:

It's true. It could be more of a memorial than her actual grave site. Either way, now we know Lucy Gray Baird has an official resting place. Here's one more reaction.

This is a good question! Why didn't this show up in the movie? I think the short answer is the movie's already long runtime of two hours and 38 minutes, making it on the longer side of 2026 movies . Thankfully Whitney Peak and Joseph Zada pointed it out for us.

articles.title: Did Loki's Doomsday Scene Create an MCU Plot Hole? Tom Hiddleston Clears Up Marvel Misunderstanding
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Loki knocking on Steve Rogers' door at the end of Avengers: Endgame Encore made some Marvel die-hards start to scratch their heads. The snippet of new footage added to the release of the blockbuster was meant to reveal to the audience how important the 2019 film really was to this year's Avengers: Doomsday, but it […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Loki knocking on Steve Rogers' door at the end of Avengers: Endgame Encore made some Marvel die-hards start to scratch their heads . The snippet of new footage added to the release of the blockbuster was meant to reveal to the audience how important the 2019 film really was to this year's Avengers: Doomsday , but it appeared to go against established MCU canon. As the obsessives know, Loki Season 2 on Disney+ ended with Tom Hiddleston's character taking on a new form as the God of Stories , holding the weaves of the multiverse in his hand at the center of the TVA. So how did he show up here?

Naturally, something that was considered canon-breaking to some has a simple explanation. Speaking with Empire , Hiddleston addressed Loki's appearance at Steve Rogers' home in the new footage, adding: “You know, he’s still got the self-duplication powers. Don’t forget that. This is some of his OG powers. He’s doing duplication casting and illusion projection in Thor .” Though Hiddleston is right and this does callback to established canon for Loki and his abilities, it's more interesting how it recontextualizes the last time we saw him .

The conclusion of Loki Season 2, literally the final image of the series, is him sitting on a throne and holding the multiverse in his hands. Given the larger context of the scene, it was easy for Marvel fans to revel in the fact that it was Loki committing the ultimate kind of sacrifice . Not only does his grasp of the various timelines seem like a healing moment for the entire multiverse, but it results in happy endings for a slew of other characters that we've gotten to know across the series. Even as the likes of Mobius appear to have moved on, Loki stands watchful over every timeline in his place.

Now that Hiddleston has confirmed that Loki isn't confined to the space we last saw him, and in fact still possesses his abilities as seen in the various Thor and Avengers movies, it stands to reason that Loki is clearly one of the most powerful characters in the entire MCU. That in mind, it's easy to see why Doctor Doom might very well have him in mind as a target for destruction , especially since his direct influence with Steve Rogers could be a cause for Doom's own personal tragedies.

It also stands to reason, thanks to Hiddleston's confirmation, that Marvel fans can't rule out the potential for Loki to show up on the other Earths that will be seen in Avengers: Doomsday . We already know that we're seeing at least three different worlds (the main 616 MCU universe, the Fox X-Men Earth, and the Fantastic Four's Earth 828), and it's possible Loki could appear on any of them since it seems he's still capable of doing it. Maybe a reunion between Loki and Thor will finally happen after their final scene eight years ago in Avengers: Infinity War .

articles.title: 3 More Fantasy TV Shows Where The Worldbuilding Is Better Than The Story, But 1 Deserved Room To Grow
articles.summary: A key part of any good fantasy story is building the world it takes place in. The confines of the fantasy genre are really only as broad as the imagination of whoever is telling the story at hand, but certain tropes and ideas seem to persist across the many popular fantasy narratives that exist in […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A key part of any good fantasy story is building the world it takes place in. The confines of the fantasy genre are really only as broad as the imagination of whoever is telling the story at hand, but certain tropes and ideas seem to persist across the many popular fantasy narratives that exist in our collective consciousness. Swords, sorcery, magic, monsters — all of these are considered staples of the fantasy worlds brought to life on our screens. The very best fantasy TV shows are those that build worlds that feel unique while still adhering to key tropes and identifiable fantasy ideas, because making a fantasy series' setting feel organic and exciting is massively important.

That said, it isn't the most important idea, though many fantasy shows lose sight of that fact. Recently, we looked at fantasy shows where the worldbuilding is better than the story , and unfortunately, the genre has no shortage of such shows. So many, in fact, that we've found three more that focused more on building a compelling world than they did on the specific narrative taking place within it. While their potential was clear, the story struggling to live up to the promise of the worldbuilding ultimately proved the downfall of each of these shows.

In many ways, The Shannara Chronicles had the potential to be one of the best fantasy shows on TV. Based on Terry Brooks' sprawling fantasy epic, The Shannara Chronicles secured then-rising star Austin Butler to play its main character, Wil. With a talented leading man and source material that ranks among the most beloved in the history of fantasy literature, the show had a massive amount of potential. Set in a fantasy world in which the remains of humanity live alongside elves, trolls, and various other magical creatures, The Shannara Chronicles had the makings of a true small-screen fantasy masterpiece.

While the world its story took place in was a good representation of the wondrous fantasy of Brooks' novels, The Shannara Chronicles ' own story left much to be desired. As incredibly compelling as the world was, the show's unimaginative use of fantasy tropes made its story feel a little cliched, with predictable romantic subplots and underdeveloped characters further hurting the show. Its general lack of success therefore seemed inevitable, and its cancellation put a final note on the series' failure to live up to its potential.

In the wake of Game of Thrones ' success, many fantasy shows sought to recreate its winning formula. A few series took historical elements and incorporated varying degrees of magic and mysticism into them, resulting in a string of shows just like Britannia . Set in the days of Roman-occupied Britain — specifically, in 43 AD — Britannia 's story follows a large ensemble cast. As one of a wave of medieval fantasy TV shows , Britannia needed to set itself apart, which it tried to do with a blend of magical elements and historical basis, all brought to life by an impressive cast featuring several celebrated actors.

The show's depiction of ancient Britain felt mysterious and unpredictable, particularly when it came to the customs, beliefs, and rituals of the land's native tribes. The care and attention that went into the worldbuilding was impressive, but sadly, Britannia 's story was nowhere near as strong. The show's increasingly convoluted plot and uneven character development proved to be a huge issue, resulting in a painfully stark imbalance between the intrigue surrounding the world's mythology and the actual story unfolding within it.

The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance was conceived as a prequel to Jim Henson's 1982 movie The Dark Crystal , offering fans a modern exploration of the events that precipitated the story of the cult fantasy film. The Netflix show aired for just one season before it was unfairly axed, contributing to its reputation as a fantasy TV show cancelled way too soon . Its inclusion on this list might raise a few eyebrows, because its story was good and earned critical acclaim, but that overlooks one simple fact: its worldbuilding was even better.

The way that Age of Resistance expands the scope of Henson's fantasy world of Thra is nothing short of wondrous. The intricacies of its fantastical cultures and complex history and mythology are truly awe-inspiring, and that's something that even its solid fantasy narrative struggled to measure up to. The story of The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance is engaging and entertaining as far as fantasy narratives go, but the world it all takes place in is infinitely more interesting and compelling, which is precisely why the show deserved a much longer run and a greater chance to grow.
